newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo tries to confront Menem on TV.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo tries to confront Menem on TV.

text.p: Renegade former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo burst into an Argentine television studio late on Thursday to confront President Carlos Menem in a live interview, but he was hustled out by producers.
"The president can't bring himself to look me in the eyes. He can't bring himself to confront me face to face," a furious Cavallo told reporters as he left the studio.

Cavallo said he wanted to speak to his former boss live on the high-rating "Hora Clave" programme about his accusations of government corruption and of the alleged judicial persecution of the one-time customs service chief Gustavo Parino.

Held back by TV personnel, Cavallo never made it in front of the cameras and could only glare at Menem from 15 feet (five meters) away. Menem never looked at him, showing no sign of being aware of his presence as the interview continued.
Since being fired by Menem in July, the minister has become the government's biggest embarrassment and regularly bombards officials and judges with accusations of corruption.

Earlier this week he said he was ashamed of having been a minister in Menem's government after Parino --- who reported to Cavallo when he was minister -- was arrested over alleged involvement with a smuggling ring.
Cavallo denounced persecution through the courts by hidden "mafias" trying to defend their corrupt interests and said Parino was a "political prisoner".
Until July, Cavallo enjoyed unprecedented power as the minister who redesigned Argentina's economy and stamped out hyperinflation.
